goals.title: Teach the sea to build
goals.critique: This is round 3's candidate again, and it fixes the two things that sank it. The three coloured sands make cause and effect visible: the plume shows where the sand went, so a player learns by watching instead of guessing. The road now starts by checking in one small surf box and one tide whether this is fun to watch, which is the right first test. The loop is still slow and indirect, though: a few placements, then up to three minutes of watching. The bell shortens the wait but doesn't add anything to do during it, and goals the player sets for themselves ('make a pink beach') are a sandbox promise, not stakes. Striped sediment that records its own history is the first image in this line that is really its own, but whether the plumes look readable or just muddy is still an assertion until the box test is filmed.

goals.title: Letters by paper plane
goals.critique: This is round 3's 'Fold it, throw it' with two real additions: targets that get harder in places you can name, and misses that stay where they fall. A tree white with fifty failed planes is a picture that tells the player's story without words, and it gives tomorrow's session a reason to look different from tonight's. The letter itself is decoration: what is written never matters to the flight or the friend, so the thing in the title isn't really a mechanic. The friends' clumsy return planes are a nice touch with nothing behind it yet. The whole bet is still unproven per-triangle aerodynamics that turn a crease into a believable bank rather than chaos. Paper litter piling up on the island records what you did without being material you build with, so the Minecraft direction is only grazed.
